values_verbatim: 0001-0099: Memory channel 1 to 99 | 0100: Programmed scan edge P1 | 0101: Programmed scan edge P2
visual_anchor: "Memory contents setting" diagram, first two cells of the byte strip, indices q and w; body text below headed "q, w Memory channel number".
notes: Selector bytes, outside the 25-byte record proper (matches IC-7610's printed (1),(2)). Clear form: append FF after the channel number in place of the data bytes e through @7.

visual_anchor: Third cell of the byte strip, index e; body text "e Select memory setting" directly under the channel-number text.
notes: Printed as one full byte (not a nibble-split cell), values 00-03 only. Byte offset 0 of the 25-byte record. Same field/position as IC-7610's byte (3) low nibble.

values_verbatim: See "Operating frequency" (Command: 00, 03, 05, 1C 03) — 10 Hz/1 Hz/1 kHz/100 Hz/10 kHz/100 kHz/10 MHz/1 MHz digits 0-9, 1000 MHz digit fixed 0, 100 MHz digit fixed 0
visual_anchor: Fourth through eighth cells of the byte strip, indices r,t,y,u,i; body text "r-i Operating frequency setting / See 'Operating frequency.'" cross-references the digit table on p.209 (folio 14-10).
notes: Byte offsets 1-5 of the record. Same shape as IC-7610 (4)-(8).

values_verbatim: 00: LSB | 05: FM | 01: USB | 07: CW-R | 02: AM | 08: RTTY-R | 03: CW | 12: PSK | 04: RTTY | 13: PSK-R || Filter: 01: FIL1 | 02: FIL2 | 03: FIL3
visual_anchor: Ninth and tenth cells of the byte strip, indices o and !0; body text "o, !0 Operating mode setting / See 'Operating mode.'" cross-references Command 01,04,06 table on p.208 (folio 14-10).
notes: Byte offsets 6-7. Same shape as IC-7610 (9)-(10). No WFM (06) code on this HF-only model.

label_verbatim: Data mode and tone type setting
values_verbatim: High nibble: 0: OFF, 1: TONE, 2: TSQL | Low nibble: 0: OFF, 1: DATA 1, 2: DATA 2, 3: DATA 3
visual_anchor: Eleventh cell of the byte strip, index !1, drawn as a two-box nibble split; body text "!1 Data mode and tone type setting" with the two value lists printed beneath the split box.
notes: Byte offset 8. Same byte position as IC-7610's (11) hi=data-mode/lo=tone_mode, but here the tone-type nibble carries only 3 values (no DTCS) vs IC-7610/IC-7100's 4-value tone_mode. Data-mode nibble (0-3) matches IC-7610's unmapped high nibble exactly.

values_verbatim: Fixed digit 0 | Fixed digit 0 | 100 Hz digit 0-2 | 10 Hz digit 0-9 | 1 Hz digit 0-9 | 0.1 Hz digit 0-9
visual_anchor: Twelfth through fourteenth cells, indices !2,!3,!4; body text "!2-!4 Repeater tone frequency setting / See 'Repeater tone/tone squelch setting.'" cross-referencing the digit strip (Command: 1B 00, 1B 01) on p.209 (folio 14-11).
notes: Byte offsets 9-11. Same shape as IC-7610 (12)-(14) tone_tx.

values_verbatim: Fixed digit 0 | Fixed digit 0 | 100 Hz digit 0-2 | 10 Hz digit 0-9 | 1 Hz digit 0-9 | 0.1 Hz digit 0-9
visual_anchor: Fifteenth through seventeenth cells, indices !5,!6,!7; body text "!5-!7 Tone squelch frequency setting", same cross-reference as !2-!4 (same referenced diagram serves both).
notes: Byte offsets 12-14. Same shape as IC-7610 (15)-(17) tone_rx. Transcribed independently; the referenced digit diagram is shared between repeater tone and tone squelch, as in the IC-7100/IC-7610 family.

values_verbatim: Up to 10 characters; see 'Codes for memory name, opening message and CLOCK2 name contents' — A-Z 41-5A | a-z 61-7A | 0-9 30-39 | space 20 | symbols ! # $ % & \ ? " ' ` ^ + - * / . , : ; = < > ( ) [ ] { } | _ ~ @
visual_anchor: Eighteenth through twenty-seventh cells, the final group of the byte strip, indices !8 through @7 (drawn with an elision run); body text "!8-@7 Memory name setting / Up to 10 characters. / See 'Codes for memory name...'" cross-referencing the character table on p.212 (folio 14-13).
notes: Byte offsets 15-24, the last 10 bytes of the 25-byte record. Same shape and width as IC-7610 (18)-(27) name.
